title: Only a few transitional links should be found, and these will be ranked as species

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Only a few transitional links should be found, and these will be ranked as species

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Given the imperfect record, one should expect to find in geological formations only a few transitional links of varying closeness between species, and even close links found in different stages of one formation will be ranked as distinct species by palaeontologists.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On the Imperfection of the Geological Record

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We ought only to look for a few links, some more closely, some more distantly related to each other; and these links, let them be ever so close, if found in different stages of the same formation, would, by most palæontologists, be ranked as distinct species.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter IX, “On the Imperfection of the Geological Record”; section “On the absence of intermediate varieties in any one formation”. Scope: fossil sequences of related species within formations

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch09-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.67

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Occurrence and taxonomy data permit broad tests, but do not directly encode morphological intermediacy or historical naming practice. Focused clades can be resolved more convincingly than the full generalization.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Within well-sampled fossil lineages and formations, quantify morphometric intermediacy, stratigraphic spacing, and taxonomic rank. Test whether intermediates are uncommon and whether close forms from successive stages are routinely assigned separate species.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Sampling and taxonomic practice vary strongly among clades and periods.

Intermediate status depends on phylogeny and chosen characters.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Occurrence records and species names are public, but morphological intermediacy is not a field in those databases and has to be assembled from clade-by-clade studies. The scarcity half is elastic, and the naming half is entangled with how palaeontologists already define species. Existing data can examine a few well-studied formations, which is a restricted slice of the stated scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Within well-sampled formations, count morphologically intermediate specimens between successive allied species and record whether close forms from different levels are given separate species names. A large roster of named intermediates inside single formations would undermine the scarcity expectation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Single formations rarely preserve continuous populations finely enough to see transitional series.

A few has no numeric cutoff, so only an extreme abundance of intermediates would count against the expectation.

Ranking close morphs as species is a taxonomic decision, so the second clause partly describes practice rather than an independent biological fact.
